question: Which diabetes products change preferred status on NY Medicaid on 10/22/2026?
assumption: Assuming NY Medicaid NYRx PDL (pub. 9/14/2026); "diabetes products" includes rapid-acting insulin and glucagon (hypoglycemia rescue). Changes are not in effect yet (today is 10/18/2026).
answer:
Assuming NY Medicaid: these changes take effect 10/22/2026, four days from today, so they aren't active yet.

| Product | Status as of 10/22/2026 |
|---|---|
| Humalog 100 U/mL vial, pen, cartridge | Preferred |
| Humalog Jr. 100 U/mL Kwikpen | Preferred |
| Insulin aspart (gen Novolog) cartridge, vial, pen | Non-preferred |
| Glucagon HCl emergency kit | Preferred |
| Gvoke pen, syringe, vial | Preferred |

The GLP-1, DPP-4, SGLT2 and long-acting insulin classes have no 10/22/2026 markers. Brand Novolog is already listed as non-preferred. The BLTG notes (Janumet and Januvia added, Farxiga removed) are separate from PDL status, and the pages I read give no effective date for them.

ny_medicaid_pdl (NY Medicaid, binding, 2026-09-14)
NYRx Preferred Drug Program (PDP) Preferred Drug List > NYS Medicaid NYRx Brand Less Than Generic (BLTG) Program
[p 77]
On April 26, 2010, NYRx, the Medicaid Pharmacy Program, implemented a new cost-containment initiative, which promotes the use of certain multisource brand name drugs when the cost of the brand name drug is less expensive than the generic equivalent.
In conformance with State Education Law, which intends that patients receive the lower cost alternative, brand name drugs included in this program:
Do not require "Dispense as Written" (DAW) or "Brand Medically Necessary" on the prescription
Have a generic copayment
Are paid at the Brand Name Drug reimbursement rate or usual and customary price, whichever is lower (SMAC/FUL are not applied)
Do not require a new prescription if the drug is removed from this program
Bosulif ® tablet, Janumet ® , Januvia ® , and Xyrem ® will be added to the program
Farxiga ® and Ravicti ® will be removed from the program

Pursuant to this program, prescription claims submitted to the Medicaid program do not require the submission of Dispense as Written/Product Selection Code of '1'; Pharmacies should submit DAW code 9 (Substitution Allowed by Prescriber but Plan Requests Brand). [p 77]
On April 26, 2010, NYRx, the Medicaid Pharmacy Program, implemented a new cost-containment initiative, which promotes the use of certain multisource brand name drugs when the cost of the brand name drug is less expensive than the generic equivalent.
In conformance with State Education Law, which intends that patients receive the lower cost alternative, brand name drugs included in this program:
Do not require "Dispense as Written" (DAW) or "Brand Medically Necessary" on the prescription
Have a generic copayment
Are paid at the Brand Name Drug reimbursement rate or usual and customary price, whichever is lower (SMAC/FUL are not applied)
Do not require a new prescription if the drug is removed from this program
Bosulif ® tablet, Janumet ® , Januvia ® , and Xyrem ® will be added to the program
Farxiga ® and Ravicti ® will be removed from the program
